paperInfo.subject: Agriculture
sourceBasis: ZIMSEC-style assessment formats and recurring syllabus areas
Original questions generated for this bank; not transcriptions of past papers
paperInfo.note: Original practice questions aligned to Agriculture syllabus coverage. They do not reproduce copyrighted past-paper text.

questions.questionText: A farmer has 4 hectares of maize and applies fertiliser at 18 kg/ha. (a) Calculate the total fertiliser required. (b) State two factors that should be considered before applying fertiliser.
questions.correctAnswer: (a) 72 kg. (b) Suitable factors include soil fertility/soil test, crop nutrient requirement, moisture conditions, correct timing and application method.
questions.explanation: Total fertiliser = 4 × 18 = 72 kg. Fertiliser decisions should consider soil and crop nutrient requirements and conditions at application.

questions.questionText: Describe how a farmer would take a representative soil sample from a cultivated field for laboratory analysis. State four precautions.
questions.correctAnswer: Use a zig-zag or representative sampling pattern; remove surface litter; take samples from a consistent depth; mix several cores; avoid unusual spots such as manure heaps and paths; use clean equipment and label the sample.
questions.explanation: Representative sampling reduces sampling error. Consistent depth, clean tools and exclusion of atypical areas improve reliability.

questions.questionText: Explain four factors that affect seed germination and state one practical way a farmer can manage each factor.
questions.correctAnswer: Water—provide adequate moisture; oxygen—avoid waterlogging; temperature—plant at a suitable time; viable seed—use mature, good-quality seed; suitable planting depth also supports emergence.
questions.explanation: Germination depends on viable seed plus suitable moisture, oxygen and temperature; management practices should create these conditions.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between preventive and curative approaches to crop disease management. Give two examples of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Preventive measures reduce disease establishment before serious infection, e.g. resistant varieties, sanitation, crop rotation or treated seed. Curative measures act after disease is present, e.g. appropriate fungicide treatment and removal of infected material.
questions.explanation: Integrated crop protection uses prevention first and targeted intervention where necessary.

questions.questionText: Describe four signs of good health in a farm animal and four signs that may indicate disease.
questions.correctAnswer: Healthy animals commonly show normal appetite, alertness, normal movement, normal respiration and appropriate body condition. Warning signs include loss of appetite, isolation, abnormal breathing, diarrhoea, unusual discharges or marked weakness.
questions.explanation: Health assessment relies on comparing behaviour, intake, movement, respiration and appearance with normal signs for the species.

questions.questionText: Explain the functions of carbohydrates, proteins, minerals and vitamins in livestock diets.
questions.correctAnswer: Carbohydrates mainly supply energy; proteins supply amino acids for growth and repair; minerals support bones, body fluids and physiological processes; vitamins regulate many metabolic processes.
questions.explanation: Balanced diets supply energy, building materials and regulatory nutrients.

questions.questionText: Explain why a vaccination programme is important in livestock production and distinguish vaccination from treatment.
questions.correctAnswer: Vaccination stimulates specific immunity before or around disease risk and reduces disease incidence. Treatment is given to an animal that is already affected or requires therapy; it does not replace a preventive vaccination programme.
questions.explanation: Vaccines are preventive biological preparations that stimulate immune responses; treatment addresses existing illness.

questions.questionText: Explain rotational grazing and give three advantages of using it on a farm.
questions.correctAnswer: Animals are moved between grazing areas according to a planned schedule, allowing rested paddocks to recover. Advantages include better pasture utilisation, reduced overgrazing, improved regrowth and potentially reduced parasite build-up.
questions.explanation: Rest periods allow pasture plants to recover and can improve utilisation and sustainability.

questions.questionText: List five routine maintenance operations for a tractor or farm machine and explain why maintenance is important.
questions.correctAnswer: Examples: check engine oil, coolant and fuel; inspect tyres; clean filters; grease moving parts; check belts, electrical connections and fasteners. Maintenance reduces breakdowns, improves safety and extends machine life.
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance detects faults early and keeps machinery operating safely and efficiently.

questions.questionText: A farmer records sales of $8,400 and variable costs of $5,100 for an enterprise. Calculate the gross margin and explain what the result means.
questions.correctAnswer: $3,300. Gross margin = gross income − variable costs = 8,400 − 5,100. It indicates the contribution available to meet fixed costs and profit.
questions.explanation: Gross margin is a useful short-term measure for comparing enterprises.

questions.questionText: Explain four factors a farmer should consider when choosing a market outlet for perishable produce.
questions.correctAnswer: Distance and transport cost; reliability of buyers; expected price; payment terms; demand and timing; handling, storage and grading requirements.
questions.explanation: Perishable products require careful consideration of time, quality, price and transaction reliability.

questions.questionText: Explain how a farm inventory record can help management decisions. Give five examples of items that may be recorded.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows quantities and values of assets and inputs, helping the farmer plan purchases and monitor losses. Items may include livestock, machinery, tools, seed, fertiliser, chemicals and feed.
questions.explanation: Accurate records support budgeting, stock control and planning.

questions.questionText: Describe five soil-conservation measures suitable for a sloping crop field and explain how each reduces erosion.
questions.correctAnswer: Contour ridges/terraces slow runoff; grass strips trap sediment; cover crops protect soil; mulching reduces raindrop impact and runoff; minimum tillage leaves residues and maintains soil structure.
questions.explanation: Conservation practices reduce runoff velocity, protect the soil surface and improve infiltration.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between weather and climate. Name four weather elements measured or observed for farm planning.
questions.correctAnswer: Weather is the short-term atmospheric condition at a place; climate describes long-term patterns. Elements include rainfall, temperature, wind speed/direction, humidity, sunshine and atmospheric pressure.
questions.explanation: Farm planning uses both short-term weather information and longer-term climate patterns.

questions.questionText: Compare sexual and asexual (vegetative) propagation in crop production. Give two advantages and two limitations of vegetative propagation.
questions.correctAnswer: Sexual propagation uses seeds and produces genetic variation; vegetative propagation uses plant parts and generally produces plants genetically similar to the parent. Advantages: rapid establishment and uniform desirable traits. Limitations: diseases may be carried over and genetic diversity is reduced.
questions.explanation: The choice depends on crop biology, disease status, desired uniformity and availability of planting material.

questions.questionText: Explain rotational grazing and give three advantages of using it on a farm.
questions.correctAnswer: Animals are moved between grazing areas according to a planned schedule, allowing rested paddocks to recover. Advantages include better pasture utilisation, reduced overgrazing, improved regrowth and potentially reduced parasite build-up.
questions.explanation: Rest periods allow pasture plants to recover and can improve utilisation and sustainability.

questions.questionText: List five routine maintenance operations for a tractor or farm machine and explain why maintenance is important.
questions.correctAnswer: Examples: check engine oil, coolant and fuel; inspect tyres; clean filters; grease moving parts; check belts, electrical connections and fasteners. Maintenance reduces breakdowns, improves safety and extends machine life.

questions.questionText: A farmer records sales of $8,400 and variable costs of $5,100 for an enterprise. Calculate the gross margin and explain what the result means.

questions.questionText: Explain four factors a farmer should consider when choosing a market outlet for perishable produce.

questions.questionText: Explain how a farm inventory record can help management decisions. Give five examples of items that may be recorded.

questions.questionText: Describe five soil-conservation measures suitable for a sloping crop field and explain how each reduces erosion.

questions.explanation: Conservation practices reduce runoff velocity, protect the soil surface and improve infiltration.

questions.questionText: Explain the difference between weather and climate. Name four weather elements measured or observed for farm planning.

questions.questionText: Compare sexual and asexual (vegetative) propagation in crop production. Give two advantages and two limitations of vegetative propagation.

questions.questionText: Describe how a farmer would take a representative soil sample from a cultivated field for laboratory analysis. State four precautions.
